newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, France seek swift restart of M.East talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia, France seek swift restart of M.East talks.

text.p: Foreign ministers Yevgeny Primakov of Russia and Herve de Charette of France on Tuesday called on Israelis and Palestinians to resume negotiations "without delay" to help restore peace in the Middle East.

"The common position of France and Russia is that it is necessary to resume without delay the process of negotiations. The principle must stay the same -- territory against peace," Primakov told a joint news conference.
"To do this it is not necessary to start again from the beginning but to keep in mind the accords that have already been signed."
Israelis and Palestinians met on Monday in U.S.-brokered talks at Erez on the Israeli-Gaza border. The talks focus on Israel's long-delayed troop redeployment in the West Bank city of Hebron.

De Charette, who also met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin during his one-day visit to Moscow, said the views of France and Russia on the Middle East were "extremely close, not to say very often identical".

The foreign ministers also discussed relations between Russia and NATO, whose planned expansion to include former Soviet satellite states in eastern and central Europe is accepted only grudgingly by Moscow.
"NATO can and must play a big role in European security but it cannot be the pivotal organisation which assumes absolutely all functions," said Primakov.

Russia has tried to link enlargement with a new treaty or charter governing all relations between the two former Cold War foes. It sees expansion as a threat to its security. NATO rejects any idea of linkage.
On Monday Russia's national security chief, Alexander Lebed, visited NATO's Brussels headquarters and urged the alliance not to rush to take on new members to the east.
